title: Dashboard detail renderer serialization loses lexical dependencies: actual Chrome confirmation
status: existing finding extended by an actual offline Chromium execution
component: UI dashboard detail overlay and VS Code detail broker
expected: Host tool/proposal detail payloads render their overlay content; a failed rendering does not suppress every usable surface.
actual: Native headless Chrome executes the generated dashboard. Clicking the Tools tab is a successful event-control. hostToolDetail raises ReferenceError DEFAULT_TOOL_DETAIL_COPY is not defined; hostProposalDetail raises ReferenceError renderCards is not defined; both overlays remain hidden with empty bodies.
rootCause: Function.toString serializes only each function body, without the surrounding constants, helpers or imports it references. Successful postMessage delivery is interpreted by the broker as successful presentation.
impact: With the broker accepting a payload, the command suppresses its standalone fallback while the browser fails before showing a detail. The command is effectively silent despite a valid model.
recommendation: Bundle a dependency-complete browser renderer or render detail HTML on the host. If broker suppression depends on presentation, acknowledge presentation or retain a recovery surface.

verification.result: Chrome exit0; real renderer, compiled SCSS, native DOM events and fake acquireVsCodeApi capture; successful Tools-tab control; two exact ReferenceErrors

relationship: Extends the already indexed UI-01, with browser evidence replacing no historical VM claim. This is not a sixth new finding.
limits: Chrome runs offline file HTML with about:blank docs and disposable profile; fake host messages and owned models. No installed VS Code webview or real backend. DBus/background stderr is retained and is not described as empty.
regressionTest: Run a real browser against the final emitted dashboard script; send both complete and minimal tool/proposal payloads and require visible populated overlays without ReferenceErrors. Test broker fallback when delivery/presentation fails.
auditorOpinion: String-rendering tests pass while browser lexical dependencies fail. Keep a small emitted-artifact browser test at this boundary rather than only testing imported renderer functions.
